sections.heading: Multiple Builder Bids over P2P
sections.summary: Potuz argued bids should only propagate if compatible with the receiver's head; Justin will create an alternative PR for Discord review.
sections.body:
- [Consensus-specs PR #5472](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5472) proposes allowing up to 3 bids from a single builder over P2P, up from the current limit of 1.
- Nico (Lodestar) explained the rationale: a builder doesn't know the proposer's view, so it needs to cover empty, full, and parent cases — hence the number 3.
  - Discovered while building a Lodestar Builder as an EPF project; current spec effectively requires 3 separate on-chain builders to cover all branches.
  - The change is fully backward compatible and non-consensus-breaking; the limit can be increased at any time.
- Potuz (Prysm) raised a counter-argument: allowing bids for non-head blocks creates a DOS vector where builders can keep increasing bid values on branches they know will never be selected, flooding the P2P gossip topic.
  - Proposed alternative: each peer should propagate only the single best bid that is compatible with its own current head.
  - Under this model, if two viable heads exist in the network, different peers naturally propagate bids for different heads, so builders don't need multiple bids per peer.
- Nico pushed back, noting that even with full agreement at slot N, not all proposer paths at slot N+1 can be covered, and forcing every node to precompute the proposer head is not current behavior.
- Potuz acknowledged the subtlety around weak blocks and GetProposerHead but maintained that filtering by head is safer and simpler.
  - Noted implementing GetProposerHead-based filtering in Prysm would be very hard; would implement with plain head instead.
- Barnabas asked whether having multiple on-chain builders would solve the problem; Potuz reiterated it doesn't address the DOS concern since the goal is to limit traffic to includeable bids.
  - Dustin noted there was a lot of effort into making builders cheap and easy.
- Decision: Justin will create a new PR implementing Potuz's head-filtering approach for comparison; further discussion to continue on Discord.

sections.heading: Attestation Rewards Bug with Missed Slots
sections.summary: A spec bug causing incorrect attestation rewards after missed slots will be fixed via PR #5473, planned to merge within 24 hours pending reviews.
sections.body:
- [Consensus-specs PR #5473](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5473) fixes a bug identified by Sproul where attestation rewards are computed incorrectly when there are missed slots before a proposal.
  - The fix returns the parent slot from `process_execution_payload_bid` and propagates it to `process_attestation` and `get_attestation_participation_flag_indices`.
- An alternative approach using a loop in fork choice to skip missing slots was considered but not preferred; Justin favors the current PR as more elegant despite touching more functions.
- Potuz approved the PR in chat, calling it "a spec bug indeed" and confirming it's an easy change for Prysm.
- Potuz raised a concern about spec test runner impact: the PR changes the signature of `process_operations`, even though the new slot parameter is only needed by `process_attestation`.
  - Justin clarified there are no `process_operations`-level tests, only individual operation tests, so only `process_attestation` tests need updating.
  - Justin committed to handling the test changes.
- Nico indicated Lodestar's Tuyen had already looked at the change from their side.
- Barnabas asked why the bug should be fixed at all, suggesting validators should only be paid if they actually propose; Justin clarified the bug affects attesters (not proposers or builders) who would not be rewarded appropriately after missed slots.
- Agreement: PR to be merged within ~24 hours if no further objections are raised in reviews.
